ownership_guard.design: A non-Copy, non-Clone guard holding exactly one SSL_SESSION reference. Constructors: SessionRef::acquire (one SSL_SESSION_up_ref; None when the object refuses a retired/destroying count) and SessionRef::adopt_cache_entry (unsafe; takes the single reference a cache entry held after that entry left the stack or its container is being released). The only ways to stop owning a reference are Drop (exactly one SSL_SESSION_free) or SessionRef::into_raw (explicit transfer to the stack that accepted a push or to a callback that accepted the reference).
sites_using_the_guard: SSL_CTX_add_session (src/ssl/ssl_sess.rs:804): the prospective cache reference is acquired before the write lock, transferred to the stack only after a successful push, and dropped after unlock for the already-cached arm and for every refusal (including a refused write lock). replaced/evicted entries are SessionRef values released after unlock.

remove_session_locked (src/ssl/ssl_sess.rs:771) now returns Option<SessionRef>. SSL_CTX_remove_session (src/ssl/ssl_sess.rs:921) releases it after the callback and outside the lock; SSL_CTX_add_session's eviction loop pushes the guards into a Vec.
SSL_CTX_flush_sessions_ex (src/ssl/ssl_sess.rs:955): Vec<SessionRef>; callback receives the borrowed pointer, the guard releases the cache reference after the callback and outside the lock.
ssl_ctx_session_cache_free (src/ssl/ssl_sess.rs:1029): remaining entries become guards whose Drop runs after the container release; no callback.

lookup_sess_in_cache (src/ssl/ssl_sess.rs:1217) now returns Option<SessionRef>; the reference is acquired under the context read lock. ssl_get_prev_session consumes it through Option and transfers the accepted reference to s->session with into_raw.

ssl_update_cache (src/ssl/ssl_sess.rs:1364): the extra reference offered to new_session_cb is a guard; a refusing callback (return 0) drops it exactly once, an accepting callback receives it through into_raw.
ownership_guard.property: A cache-held or lookup-acquired reference cannot be dropped twice (Drop runs once per guard) and cannot be retained after removal (the detached entry is moved into a guard). A refused insert after partially acquiring references unwinds exactly once. The public SSL_SESSION_up_ref / SSL_SESSION_free ABI is unchanged.

scratch_key_decision.old: lookup_sess_in_cache fabricated a whole SslSession with core::mem::zeroed() and wrote the three compared fields; its validity was documented, not structural.
scratch_key_decision.new: SessionKey (src/ssl/ssl_sess.rs:578-645) holds exactly ssl_version, session_id_length and session_id, is written field-by-field by from_id, and is compared by matches(). cache_find now takes &SessionKey; of_session builds a key from a live session.
scratch_key_decision.why: AGENTS §2: zeroed storage is not automatically a valid T. The old probe's validity depended on every present and future field of SSL_SESSION being zero-valid, which is a property of the whole type, not of the compared fields. A key-only type eliminates the obligation instead of documenting it: no storage is reinterpreted as a session, and a future field addition cannot silently invalidate the probe.
scratch_key_decision.safety_improvement: matches() refuses a stored session_id_length wider than SSL_MAX_SSL_SESSION_ID_LENGTH instead of reading past the array (the authority's memcmp would read out of bounds; AGENTS §17). The comparator's length-0 equality is preserved.

concurrency_verdict.what_establishes_it: lookup_sess_in_cache holds ctx->lock in read mode across cache_find and SSL_SESSION_up_ref; SSL_CTX_add_session, SSL_CTX_remove_session and SSL_CTX_flush_sessions_ex all take the same lock in write mode. The crate's CRYPTO_RWLOCK is reader/writer: readers share, writers exclude both (src/runtime/thread.rs:31-68). The cache's reference therefore cannot be released between the find and the acquire. After unlock the returned SessionRef is the caller's own reference and survives any later eviction, removal or flush.
concurrency_verdict.residual: Eviction, removal and flushing write the non-atomic session bookkeeping fields not_resumable and owner under the write lock, while a thread that already owns a reference reads them (and the session payload) without any lock. Those accesses are a data race in the Rust memory model and formally in C; the authority has the same structure. Proving this needs a design change (atomic bookkeeping or protecting every reader), which S57 does not make. No lock was added that the authority does not take. Recorded in the module header under 'Concurrency: what is established and what is not'.

tests.name: cache_lifecycle_tests::ssl_sess_reentrant_new_session_cb_mutates_an_unlocked_cache
tests.asserts: new_session_cb runs outside the cache lock (lock probe free), its re-entrant SSL_CTX_add_session returns 1 and inserts the other session, the callback accepts and releases its own extra reference, and the cache ends with exactly {current, other} at the expected reference counts

tests.name: cache_lifecycle_tests::ssl_sess_refusing_new_session_cb_leaves_the_cache_unchanged
tests.asserts: a callback returning 0 takes no reference and changes nothing; the cache still holds exactly the current session; refs are connection + cache (2), proving the offered reference was released exactly once

tests.name: cache_lifecycle_tests::ssl_sess_lookup_reference_survives_cache_replacement
tests.asserts: a lookup guard held while a different object replaces the same key keeps the incumbent alive (3 refs -> 2 after replacement), the cache points at the replacement by address, the incumbent's owner is cleared, and the in-flight session is still readable at its own address

tests.name: cache_lifecycle_tests::ssl_sess_refused_add_releases_the_partially_acquired_reference_once
tests.asserts: with the write lock already held by this thread, SSL_CTX_add_session returns 0 after having called SSL_SESSION_up_ref; refs return to 1, the cache is empty, owner is NULL, and the address-identity ex-data destructor probe fires exactly once when the last reference is released

tests.name: cache_lifecycle_tests::ssl_sess_lookup_uses_a_key_value_not_a_zeroed_session
tests.asserts: SessionKey matches on ssl_version + id, rejects a different id/version, truncates an over-long id at the array width, preserves length-0 keys, and refuses an over-wide stored session_id_length without reading out of bounds

tests.name: cache_lifecycle_tests::ssl_sess_canary_detects_an_unreleased_partial_acquisition
tests.asserts: negative control: an unguarded partial acquisition (manual up_ref with no matching release) keeps the block live, so the address-identity destructor probe reports no release; releasing the simulated extra reference makes it fire once

tests.name: pre-existing ssl_sess / cache_lifecycle_tests / alias_ownership_tests / refcount_reentrancy_tests
